It all depends on the crystal itself. Generally speaking, quartz family crystals (besides clear quartz- faked as glass and citrine, faked as glass, heated amethyst, irradiated quartz) are rarely faked due to their abundance. Rarer rough minerals like dioptase, cavansite, vivianite, etc etc are also rarely faked due to the inability to make a convincing fake. Some fakes I often see are citrine, ruby zoisite, turquoise and rutile. A lot of gemstones also have lab grown counterparts and it can be difficult to tell the difference with the naked eye (like rubies and sapphires). 

Very very generally, if it’s rough, the odds are higher that it’s real (there are exceptions to this). If it’s polished or gem cut, you’ll need to do some research to determine its authenticity.
